findings.text: the base-side comparison ran the head's test files against the base library: pytest is given a relative "tests/" and the script never cds into $TREE, so the collection root is the worker's worktree, and the manifest's explanation is its corollary rather than a finding - the base's own copy of tests/test_rollback_asks_head.py fails on replay (PYTHONPATH=<archive> TMPDIR=/tmp: 7 failed, 5 passed, the same seven ids merged-before.log records) while the base log's 225 ids hold no rollback id at all, which is exactly what collecting the head's all-passing copy yields.

the "11 failures" counter reproduces nowhere: the recorded base-side measurements are 7 (the same file in a git checkout, merged-before.log) and no log in this run contains an eleven-failure figure, so a number with no instrument behind it is carried into the evidence_inputs the coordinator will write back.

the "~5,200 live pointers are re-read and re-parsed" mechanism is a run-directory count under the pointer store's name: live/*.json holds 33 files (measured 2026-09-22T11:37Z) while runs/ holds 5,245 (5,198 at 10:26Z, the number the record uses), _list_live_records reads live/*.json only (reckon/crew/runs.py:417-421), and the stalled case cannot depend on that store because its fixture pins RECKON_HOME (tests/test_crew_attempt_accounting.py:13-17) - in my isolated rerun with RECKON_HOME at a temp path the case stalls identically (timeout 150, exit 124, no output), so the fleet-scale driver the record and its follow_on assert is not what the measurement shows.

the fence-time caveat does not reproduce either: sacct puts job 1275671 at 10:47:38-10:55:43Z and job 1275673 at 10:47:47-10:55:41Z against a dispatch at 10:25:50Z, so the fence expired at 11:05:50Z and the last stream event is 11:08:26Z - an overrun of about 2.6 minutes, with both runs finished roughly ten minutes before the fence passed rather than in flight when it did.

the cumulative anchor and docs/figures/crew-runtime-positive-controls/suite-failure-sets.svg carry the same unsupported figures and the same base-side comparison, so every later reader of the durable record inherits the 5,200-pointer mechanism and a delta that was measured across the wrong test tree.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit - 92fe8b9d is docs-only (+103/-0); the measurement lives outside git, where I read both log headers, the four id files, both run scripts and the rolled-up evidence anchor section.
item_verdicts.done_when: every clause of the evidence fence is checkable in the head log and holds - revision, tree and command on its first lines, a scheduler line naming all_debug job 1275671 with TMPDIR=/tmp, the deselected case named with its reason, failing ids listed by nodeid, counts and EXIT=1 as the last lines, and the log kept unedited with the non-zero exit reported rather than retried into a pass.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal asks the current main revision to carry a measured suite result and a named failure set; /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/main-suite-at-head.log holds exactly that at 1a6dc6fc (224 failed, 5421 passed, 68 skipped, 11 errors, 1 deselected, EXIT=1, every failing nodeid listed) and the incident file is reported separately at 12 passed - but the comparison that licenses "adds no failing test" ran the head's test files against the base's library, so it measured base library code rather than the base revision.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it carries the commit, every log path, both suite blocks with their ids and the read negative control, and it declares the unbuilt ADDED-direction positive control itself - but three supporting figures do not reproduce and its explanation for the base run's rollback file is refuted by replaying that file.
item_verdicts.write_paths: git show --stat 92fe8b9d lists exactly the three declared paths - the cumulative evidence anchor (+73), docs/figures/crew-runtime-positive-controls/suite-failure-sets.svg (+27) and three lines in the plan (+3) - 103 insertions and zero deletions, no source file and no plan meta line touched.

justifications.durability: the anchor and figure are committed cumulatively and the logs sit in the reports and run directories rather than /tmp, but the comparative claim rests on a base log whose tests tree will not reproduce, and the record itself states that no positive control for an ADDED failure was built.
justifications.evidence: the failure-set files were read id by id, but run-base-suite.sh:22 hands pytest a relative tests/ with no cd into $TREE so both logs total the same 5,724 outcomes over different test trees, and the 11-failure, ~5,200-pointer and ten-minute-overrun figures each fail to reproduce or are refuted.
justifications.fit: the log header, the anchor section and a set-shaped SVG match this repository's conventions for a measurement node, but "live pointer" is used for a count of run directories the pointer store never holds, and the follow_on's proposed repair is built on that count.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the head result is real and I reproduced its key facts - the log header, the id files, the EXIT line and the incident file at 12 passed (my own rerun: 12 passed in 3.85s) - while the mis-specified base side leaves "adds no failing test" established against the base library only.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat 92fe8b9d lists exactly the three declared paths with zero deletions, no plan meta line in the diff and no source file reached, the run-directory logs and scripts being the node's own gate artifacts.
